results.title: HFlow: Scalable multimodal data pipelines for robotics
results.content:
Hi Product Hunt,  
  
We built HFlow because robotics teams are collecting more hours of video data than they can handle. Each episode can contain camera streams, robot state, actions, timestamps, and metadata. As a corpus grows, one-off scripts make it hard to answer basic questions: Did a camera freeze? Did streams drift out of sync? Which version of a check ran? Can we reproduce the dataset we used?  
  
HFlow turns that work into a pipeline. Transforms, checks, labels, and enrichments stay yours. HFlow handles orchestration, storage, versioning, and curation around them. It writes canonical MCAP episodes with provenance, records quality evidence in a Parquet catalog, and builds version-pinned manifests with DuckDB. [...] The core lifecycle works end to end today. You can run the included quickstart locally  
without Docker, Airflow, robot hardware, or an external service.  
  
HFlow is Apache-2.0 licensed and built in public by Hebbian Robotics (YC S26). If you work with robotics or physical AI data, try the quickstart and tell us where your current data workflow loses the most context. Is it ingestion, quality control, provenance, or curation?  
  
HFlow is built by Hebbian Robotics and is part of Y Combinator’s Summer 2026 batch.

# Building embodied AI data pipelines for scalable learning

May 20, 2026

Embodied AI systems must perceive their environment, process information from multimodal sensors, make decisions, and execute actions in real time. This requires a scalable data infrastructure capable of supporting complex robotics training workflows.

Therefore, organizations developing robotic systems are investing in specialized robotics data workflows and automated processing pipelines. They support large-scale data collection, synchronization, annotation, storage, validation, and model training.

## Quick Take [...] Embodied AI pipelines support:

 Continuous sensor data loading.
 Real-time synchronization.
 Temporal data processing.
 Multimodal alignment.
 Large-scale annotation workflows.
 Real-world modeling and integration.

The goal is to create a scalable infrastructure that allows robotics models to learn from complex physical interactions.

## Core components of embodied AI data pipelines

Robotics data workflows depend on interconnected pipeline components that support data collection, synchronization, processing, and training. [...] ## Quick Take

 Embodied AI systems require specialized multimodal data pipelines.
 Robotic data workflows support scalable acquisition, annotation, and training.
 AI-based data engineering in robotics focuses on synchronization, storage, and preprocessing.
 Simulation environments improve scalability but pose challenges for data transfer.
 Continuous validation and modular infrastructure are essential for robust AI robotic systems.

## What are embodied AI data pipelines?

Embodied AI data pipelines are structured systems that manage the flow of robotics data from collection to model training and deployment. These pipelines are used to process multimodal sensor streams and large-scale robot interaction data.

results.title: AXIS: A Growable Community-Driven Data Engine for Scalable Robot Manipulation | alphaXiv
results.content:
Existing pipelines are often static, meaning they provide a fixed set of trajectories that do not evolve over time. This centralized approach limits the speed at which datasets can grow, often leaving them lagging behind the models they are meant to train. Furthermore, collecting data on physical robots is expensive and difficult to scale. While simulation offers a promising alternative, setting up high-fidelity simulators often requires substantial local compute resources and manual environment design.

AXIS Overview: A Growable Community-Driven Data Engine Figure 1: The AXIS framework integrates automated task generation, web-based community teleoperation, data refinement, and realistic augmentation to create a continuously expanding data engine for robot learning. [...] These findings suggest that the diversity of the "community-driven" demonstrations—which include various human strategies and correction behaviors—contributes to a broader generalization that goes beyond simple visual randomization. By capturing the nuances of how humans solve tasks, AXIS provides a richer learning signal for VLA models.

## Significance and Future Directions

The AXIS framework provides a scalable alternative to the traditional manual, centralized data collection methods in robotics. By integrating automated task synthesis with a low-barrier web teleoperation system, it enables a "growable" dataset that can keep pace with the needs of modern AI models.

### Key Contributions Recap:

results.title: AXIS: A Growable Community-Driven Data Engine for Scalable Robot Manipulation
results.content:
A fundamental limitation of existing manipulation data pipelines is that data collection remains largely closed and centralized. Expert operators or dedicated teams gather demonstrations on local hardware, process them offline, and release the resulting dataset as a fixed benchmark [5, 11]. While this paradigm offers strong control over data quality, it does not naturally support continual task expansion, broad community participation, or rapid iteration as robot capabilities evolve. Scaling robot learning instead requires data infrastructure that can continuously expand along multiple dimensions, including tasks, objects, scenes, contributors, visual conditions, and physical variations. [...] Learning effective robot manipulation policies requires diverse, high-quality demonstrations, yet existing data pipelines are often difficult to scale because they rely on specialized hardware, centralized operators, or fixed task suites.
We present AXIS, a growable community-driven data engine and benchmark for scalable robot learning, which enables browser-based teleoperation for large-scale demonstration collection, automatically generates and validates new manipulation tasks, and transforms community-collected demonstrations into training-ready data through automated success checking, quality filtering, trajectory smoothing, and visual and physics-based augmentation. [...] Table 4 summarizes representative robot manipulation datasets spanning real-world robotics, simulation environments, and large-scale embodied learning benchmarks. Existing datasets generally emphasize either large-scale real-world data collection (e.g., RoboNet, Open X-Embodiment, DROID, and RoboMIND) or highly controlled simulation benchmarks with expert demonstrations (e.g., LIBERO and PartInstruct). While these datasets have substantially advanced robot learning, their collection pipelines often require specialized robotic hardware, expert operators, or centralized infrastructure, limiting scalability and accessibility.
